title: A Continuation of the Reminiscences of John Watson, M.D.
question: Today, can Jefferson Hope tell his whole story before his heart gives out?
light: low raking lamplight, deep black shadow

station_desk.described: Interior, inside a small bare charge room at a London police station on a March night in 1881, the camera within the room with whitewashed brick walls closed on all four sides: a high dark wooden clerk's desk with a sloping top and a ledger open on it, a gas jet burning in a brass bracket on the left wall above the desk, a plain wooden bench along the right wall, a heavy panelled door in the far wall; the gas jet is the only light and it comes from the left, low and yellow, on the desk, the ledger and the faces nearest it, and leaves the right wall, the bench and the corners black
station_desk.landmark_size: is half the height of the frame
station_desk.route: from the high desk across the bare boards to the panelled door
station_desk.geometry: The high wooden desk stands at the LEFT third of the frame with the gas jet burning above it at the TOP LEFT. The panelled door stands in the far wall at the CENTRE of the upper third, black. The bench runs along the RIGHT edge in black shadow and the bare boards fill the BOTTOM third. The gas light reaches the CENTRE of the frame and dies at the RIGHT third.

euston_platform.described: Interior, inside the great iron-roofed train shed of Euston Station on a March evening in 1881, the camera on the platform under the glass roof: a long stone platform beside a line of dark railway carriages, iron columns in a row down the platform's edge, a porter's barrow stacked with trunks, steam drifting under the roof; the gas lamps hung on the columns are the only light and they come from the right, low and yellow, on the steam, the trunks and the near faces, and leave the carriages, the roof ironwork and the far end of the shed black
euston_platform.landmark: the porter's barrow stacked with trunks
euston_platform.landmark_size: is half the height of the frame
euston_platform.route: from the porter's barrow along the platform to the barrier at the far end
euston_platform.geometry: The line of dark carriages runs along the LEFT edge of the frame into the distance. The iron columns stand in a row down the RIGHT third with the gas lamps on them. The porter's barrow stands at the BOTTOM RIGHT and the platform runs from the BOTTOM CENTRE to the black far end at the CENTRE of the frame. The glass roof is black across the TOP edge above the steam.
euston_platform.crowd: Travellers in dark coats walk along the platform at a walking pace in twos and threes, a porter in a peaked cap pushes a barrow of trunks, and steam drifts between the iron columns.

cab_night_rain.described: A wet London street of dark brick houses at one in the morning in March 1881, blowing hard and raining in torrents: a four-wheeled cab with a dark bay horse standing at the kerb, the cabman hunched on the box, the cobbles running with water under a black night sky, a single gas lamp on an iron post at the kerb; the gas lamp is the only light and it comes from the right, low and yellow, on the wet cobbles, the slanting rain, the horse's streaming flank and the cab's wet panels, and leaves the house fronts and the far street black
cab_night_rain.landmark: the gas lamp on its iron post
cab_night_rain.landmark_size: is half the height of the frame
cab_night_rain.route: from the gas lamp at the kerb along the wet street to the garden gate of the empty house
cab_night_rain.geometry: The gas lamp on its iron post stands at the RIGHT third of the frame with its light on the wet cobbles. The cab and the bay horse stand along the kerb across the CENTRE of the frame. The dark house fronts fill the LEFT edge and the black street runs to the CENTRE of the upper third. The rain slants across the lamplight from the TOP RIGHT to the BOTTOM LEFT.

brixton_front_room.described: Interior, inside the empty front room of a shut-up house in the Brixton Road at one in the morning, March 1881, the camera within the room with walls closed on all four sides: bare floorboards thick with dust, walls of cheap flaring yellow paper peeling in strips and blotched with mildew, a mantelpiece of imitation white marble on the left wall, a single tall curtainless window in the far wall black with night and streaming with rain, a panelled door in the right wall; a single wax candle in a man's hand is the only light and it comes from the candle alone, low and yellow, on the faces and hands nearest it and on the peeling paper beside it, and leaves the window, the corners and the ceiling black

brixton_front_room.route: from the panelled door across the bare boards to the tall window
brixton_front_room.geometry: The tall rain-streaked window stands in the far wall at the CENTRE of the upper third, grey. The white marble mantelpiece stands along the LEFT wall at the LEFT third. The panelled door is at the RIGHT edge and the bare dusty boards fill the BOTTOM third. The candle's light reaches the middle of the frame and the ceiling is black across the TOP edge.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: We drove him to the station in his own cab, and he came as quiet as a lamb.

lines.speaker: police_inspector
lines.text: Have you anything to say? It will be taken down.

lines.speaker: jefferson_hope
lines.text: I may never be tried.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: I put my hand on his chest. Inside, something throbbed like an engine in a shed.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: You have an aortic aneurism!

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: He sat down, and told us the whole of it as calmly as a man reading a timetable.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: For two weeks he had driven behind Drebber and Stangerson, and never once found them apart.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Then at Euston they missed the Liverpool train, and Drebber went off alone into the night.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Hope drove him from one gin palace to the next, until the man could barely stand.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: In his pocket was a little box with two pills in it, and only one was poisoned.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: All the way, John Ferrier and Lucy walked ahead of the horse in the rain, one each side.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: At Brixton Road he woke his passenger, and walked him up the garden to the empty house.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: It was black inside. Hope struck a match, and lit a wax candle he had brought.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Drebber stamped about the dust, grumbling at the dark, and waiting to be shown his room.

lines.speaker: jefferson_hope
lines.text: Now then, Enoch Drebber. Look at my face, and tell me who I am.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: The drink went out of his eyes, and the horror came into them. He knew.

lines.speaker: enoch_j_drebber
lines.text: Would you murder me?

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Hope held out the box. Drebber was to choose, and Hope would swallow the pill that was left.

lines.speaker: jefferson_hope
lines.text: Let us see if there is justice upon the earth.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: When the poison took hold, Hope held Lucy's wedding ring up before his eyes.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: It was quick. He threw out his hands, and fell, and never moved again.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Stangerson he found two days later, and gave the same choice. The man flew at his throat.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: When he stopped, nobody spoke. There was only the scratch of Lestrade's pencil.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Holmes had one question left: who had come to our rooms for the ring?

lines.speaker: jefferson_hope
lines.text: I can tell my own secrets, but not other people's.

lines.speaker: police_inspector
lines.text: On Thursday he goes before the magistrates. Until then, he is mine.
